gitCommit.subject: Give auto-sync real calculation rules instead of a silent no-op
gitCommit.body:
Give auto-sync real calculation rules instead of a silent no-op

A transaction type with no rule makes calculate_amount_for_transaction return
nil, and every caller reads nil as "skip" — so auto-sync could be on, with
categories and accounts set, and link nothing at all, forever, with the toggle
reading Activada. Manual linking hit the same wall and logged a warning that
claimed the type was "ignore" when it had never been set.

Categories and bank accounts were already required for auto-sync; the rules
that decide what it actually does were neither required nor defaulted. The
defaults existed in two other places (FinancialTemplate, and mergeCalc on
mobile) — applied where it did not matter and skipped where it did.

The models now own DEFAULT_CALCULATION, FinancialTemplate references it, and
before_validation fills only the missing keys so an explicit "ignore" survives.
All four set to ignore with auto-sync on is now rejected: that combination can
never link anything. Production has no record in that state, so this rejects
nothing that exists, and none with missing keys, so no backfill is needed —
before_validation heals any stragglers on their next save.

The advanced panel now opens when auto-sync is on. Collapsing the rules that
define the automation is how a record ends up syncing nothing in the first
place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
